title: 10 Most Popular Attractions in Krabi 2026 — Landmarks, Beaches, Temples, and Markets Worth Coming Back to Every Time | ThailandAddict
metaDesc: The 10 most popular attractions in Krabi 2026 — Black Crab Square, Khao Khanab Nam, Railay Beach, Wat Tham Suea, Wat Bang Thong, Emerald Pool, Hot Springs, Ao Nang Night Market — with entry fees, directions, and opening hours

eyebrow: See it like a local · Updated 2026
intro:
Krabi is more than just beautiful sea — it has limestone mountains rising from the water, white-sand beaches, hilltop temples, and a seaside night market for an evening stroll, all in one province.

We picked 10 attractions that people keep coming back to on every Krabi trip, from city landmarks to the emerald pool deep in the forest. Read through and plan your trip right here.
chips: 🦀 Black Crab Square + Khao Khanab Nam — the city pair
🏖️ Railay Beach — clear water, limestone cliffs
💚 Emerald Pool + Hot Springs, Khlong Thom

blocks.html:
Krabi's charm is that you can do many different types of travel in a single day. In the morning, climb Wat Tham Suea for a temple visit on a hilltop. Mid-morning, stop at Black Crab Square by the river with Khao Khanab Nam as your backdrop. Afternoon, take a longtail boat over to Railay Beach, where limestone cliffs wrap around white sand. In the evening, come back to stroll Ao Nang Landmark or Krabi Walking Street with seafood and a sea breeze. For those who want full nature immersion, drive out to Khlong Thom to float in the emerald-green pool and soak in the hot-spring pools in the forest — like a natural jacuzzi. This is a province that suits beach relaxation, nature hiking, temple visits, and photography all in one trip.

Many places on this list are the city's defining images. Black Crab Square and Khao Khanab Nam are the pair of symbols that have appeared on every Krabi postcard for years. Wat Mahathat Wachira Mongkol in Ao Luek has a golden chedi over 95 meters tall, inspired by Bodh Gaya, on more than 100 rai surrounded by mountains. Wat Tham Suea is famous for its 1,237-step climb to a 360-degree panorama of Krabi town. Railay Beach is a rock-climbing mecca that people fly in from around the world to attempt. Together, these are 10 places that consistently live up to expectations — go and see for yourself.

blocks.name: Black Crab Square (Black Crab Monument)
blocks.area: Khanab Nam Pier, Pak Nam, Mueang Krabi, Krabi
blocks.signature: Gold-toned black crab family sculptures on the river, with Khao Khanab Nam as the backdrop — the city's top check-in landmark
blocks.descHtml:
Black Crab Square — officially called the Black Crab Monument — is Krabi town's most recognized landmark, and practically every visitor who arrives in the city makes a stop here. The focal point is a family of black-crab sculptures in gold-toned bronze: a large mother crab with a shell about two meters wide, plus three smaller crabs raising their claws, all set on the Krabi River bank. The backdrop is Khao Khanab Nam, two limestone peaks rising from the water that are the province's defining symbol. A short distance away is also the Eagle Monument (the eagle representing the richness of Krabi's mangrove estuaries), another photo point. Works for anyone wanting the city's most recognizable check-in shot — couples, families, and casual walkers alike.

The highlight is the classic shot: stand with the crab sculptures and frame Khao Khanab Nam behind you. The best light is early morning with a cool breeze, and late afternoon approaching sunset when the light is soft. Many reviews mention coming out for a riverside morning run or walk — the mangrove path along the water is refreshing and green. In the evenings, people sit along the river and a small market with street food appears on the opposite side, easy to walk across for something to eat while watching the view.

Free entry, free roadside parking, open public space with no admission fee or timing restrictions. Located at Khanab Nam Pier, Pak Nam subdistrict, right on the Krabi River in the city center — walking distance from the Krabi Walking Street and the main city night market. The combination of an iconic photo stop and easy evening onward access makes this the natural first stop of any Krabi city visit. Google score of 4.5 from several thousand reviews.

Worth knowing: this is a quick photo stop, not a half-day destination. Most people finish in under an hour and move on. Midday sun is strong and there's minimal shade — morning and late afternoon are more comfortable. Allow time to walk the riverside market or the walking street nearby to make the most of the area.
mustOrder: Photo with the black crab sculptures and Khao Khanab Nam behind
Eagle Monument nearby
Riverside evening stroll
Street food from the market on the opposite bank
blocks.bestFor: City landmark check-in — morning or late afternoon by the river

blocks.name: Khao Khanab Nam
blocks.signature: Twin limestone peaks flanking the river mouth, boat through a mangrove tunnel, explore stalactite caves, views iconic enough for a postcard
blocks.descHtml:
Khao Khanab Nam is a pair of limestone peaks approximately 100 meters tall, standing on either side of the Krabi River mouth just in front of the city — the visual gateway and most recognizable image of the province. Anyone coming to Krabi who wants to see the real thing of the postcard view needs to come here. The starting point is a longtail boat from Chao Fa Pier in the city center — a 15-minute ride at a relaxed pace. Works well for nature lovers, families, couples, and anyone who wants a beautiful photograph without a long journey.

The highlights not to miss: gliding through the mangrove tunnel with dense nipa palms on both sides — stepping into a different, quieter world. Then climb stone stairs up into the caves on the mountains. Inside are stalactites and stalagmites with archaeological history: prehistoric cave paintings several thousand years old, ancient human skeletons, and a sculpture of a giant skeleton wrapped in a serpent that is one of the most photographed details. Another favorite is standing at the cave mouth looking out over the river and the city — a view that stays in the memory. In late afternoon, bats pour out of the caves in great numbers.

The site itself is free to enter. Your main cost is the boat — a private longtail is around 500 THB (for a group), or join others for roughly the low hundreds per person. Most reviews call it very good value for the time spent (one to two hours). Google score of 4.5 from several hundred reviews reflects consistent satisfaction. The location recently became even more well-known as a filming location for Jurassic World Rebirth.

Worth knowing: the most comfortable season is November to April — clear skies and calm water make for better photography. Come mid-morning to noon for the best water level for the mangrove passage. Bring a torch for the caves. Wear shoes you can manage stone stairs in. Watch your bags — monkeys in the area are known for grabbing things. Negotiate the boat price before boarding — standard practice here.
mustOrder: Longtail boat through the mangrove tunnel
Climb into the stalactite caves — prehistoric paintings and ancient skeletons
Photo of the twin limestone peaks flanking the river
Watch bats fly out of the caves at dusk
blocks.bestFor: First-time visitors wanting to see the iconic landmark in person

blocks.name: Wat Tham Suea (Tiger Cave Temple)
blocks.signature: Climb 1,237 stairs to the summit, 360-degree views of Krabi town from the top, large Buddha image and chedi, sunrise and sea of mist at dawn
blocks.descHtml:
If you come to Krabi wanting a panoramic city view, Wat Tham Suea is the landmark most people are unwilling to skip. The temple is in Ban Tham Suea, Krabi Noi subdistrict, about 5–6 km from the city center. Originally a forest area with a cave where locals reportedly saw tigers — which gave it the name Tiger Cave Temple. Today it is a meditation practice temple on over 200 rai of grounds. The right fit for hikers, people who love views, and merit-makers who want both the spiritual experience and a beautiful image to take home.

The highlight everyone talks about is the summit staircase — the sign says 1,237 steps (some reviews count approximately 1,260), rising to about 600 meters above sea level. At the top: a large chedi and a Buddha image, with a 360-degree view of Krabi town, limestone mountains, and the sea below. Many visitors set out before dawn to wait for sunrise and the sea of mist in the morning. Sunsets are equally spectacular from a different angle. Reviews consistently say it is genuinely tiring — the stairs are steep and the step height varies — but arriving at the top makes the effort disappear immediately.

Free to visit; there is a donation box for temple upkeep. Budget mainly goes on drinking water and leg strength. The temple is open from early morning, around 05:00–06:00, through the evening to approximately 18:00. At the base there are also a cave for meditation and a large Guan Yin image to venerate before the climb. The combination of a temple visit, a physical challenge, and a high-altitude view is what has kept this on every Krabi list.

Before you go: wear shoes you can climb in. Dress modestly — this is an active temple. Bring plenty of water. Go slowly and take breaks. Most importantly, be alert around monkeys on the way up — they are numerous and known for grabbing food, phones, glasses, and bags carried openly. Keep everything secured before you start climbing.
mustOrder: Climb all 1,237 stairs to the summit of Khao Kaeo
360-degree view of Krabi town from the top
Large chedi and Buddha image at the summit
Venerate the Guan Yin image and the meditation cave at the base
blocks.bestFor: Hikers and view-chasers — come for sunrise or morning sea of mist
blocks.libCredit: Photo: Wat Tham Suea · Stefan Fussan · Wikimedia Commons · CC BY-SA 3.0

blocks.name: Railay Beach
blocks.signature: White sand flanked by limestone cliffs — West Railay for swimming and sunset, East Railay for rock climbing, and a walk through to Phra Nang Cave Beach
blocks.descHtml:
Railay Beach is a small peninsula in Krabi cut off from the mainland by tall limestone cliffs, reachable only by boat — which gives the whole place a feel of stepping into another world. Well suited for those who want a beautiful beach, nature lovers, couples after a sunset, and serious rock climbers who travel from around the world to climb here. The peninsula is clearly divided into two sides: West Railay with fine white sand and clear water, ideal for swimming and views, and East Railay with mangrove and cliff faces, the go-to zone for rock climbing.

The experience not to miss is walking from West Railay through to Phra Nang Cave Beach, which many reviews nominate as the most beautiful beach in the area — fine sand, emerald-green water, a spirit shrine inside the cave, and a front-row view of people climbing the cliffs. In the evening, come back to the west side to watch the sunset — the light hitting the cliff faces and the water together makes for photographs that are easy to get and hard to improve. Anyone up for short hiking can reach the Railay viewpoint or the hidden lagoon further inside.

The beach itself is free. Your main cost is the longtail boat from Ao Nang or Ao Nam Mao Pier, approximately 100–150 THB one way per person (boats usually wait to fill before departing), a 15–20 minute ride. Food and drinks on the beach are noticeably more expensive than in Ao Nang, since everything is brought in by boat. Bring cash and water. The beach is enjoyable all day but the most beautiful times are early morning and late afternoon when crowds are thinner. Best season is November to March, when the sea is calm and the sky is clear.

Why it keeps appearing on every Krabi list: it packages a world-class beach, accessible rock climbing, a cave to walk to, and some of the best sunset conditions in the province all in one peninsula. Worth knowing: midday is busy and crowded. The East Railay side at low tide is muddy and not suitable for swimming — check tide times before planning a walk across to Phra Nang Cave. Wear walking shoes and bring water.
mustOrder: Watch the sunset from West Railay
Walk through to Phra Nang Cave Beach
Watch rock climbing on East Railay
Hike up to the viewpoint / hidden lagoon
blocks.bestFor: Krabi beach trip — sunset views, couples, and rock climbers

blocks.name: Emerald Pool and Hot Springs, Khlong Thom
blocks.signature: Emerald-green freshwater pools in a rainforest to swim in, and naturally warm springs flowing into rock basins like a natural jacuzzi — usually visited together in one trip
blocks.descHtml:
For visitors who want a break from the sea and a swim in cool freshwater in the middle of a rainforest, this is the answer. The Emerald Pool is a natural pool inside the Khao Pra-Bang Khram Wildlife Sanctuary with water so clear you can see the sandy bottom and small fish below. The emerald color comes from mineral content in the water. You can float in it like a natural spa. A short distance away, the Hot Springs flow over layered limestone basins at around 40–50 degrees Celsius — like a jacuzzi that nature put together. Most visitors combine both in a single trip. Well suited for families, couples, and nature enthusiasts who want a relaxing soak.

The highlights: getting into the Emerald Pool fully — all three pools (Sa Kaeo, Sa Morakot, and Sa Nam Phut) — which change shade with the light at different times of day. Then continue to the Hot Springs and alternate between soaking in the warm water and cooling off in the cold stream beside it. Reviewers note that the rocks have a mineral coating that is not particularly slippery — easier to step on than expected.

Entry fees are accessible: Thais pay tens of baht per site; foreigners around 200 THB at the Emerald Pool, plus a small vehicle fee. Open approximately 08:30–16:30 daily. Located in Khlong Thom Nuea subdistrict, Khlong Thom district, about 50 km from Krabi town — drive yourself or book a day tour. Google score of 4.3 from over 10,000 reviews reflects widespread enjoyment.

Worth knowing: tour groups arrive late morning to noon and it gets crowded, especially at the hot springs which have limited pool space. Arriving right when it opens means a more peaceful experience and better photographs. Bring a swimsuit, non-slip shoes, and insect repellent — you'll get more out of the visit.
mustOrder: Float in the emerald-green pool
Soak in the hot-spring rock-basin pools (natural jacuzzi)
Walk through Sa Kaeo and Sa Nam Phut pools
Cool down in the cold stream beside the hot springs
blocks.bestFor: Nature swimmers — arrive early before tour groups arrive

blocks.name: Ao Nang Landmark Night Market
blocks.area: Ao Nang, near Nopparat Thara Beach, Ao Nang, Mueang Krabi, Krabi
blocks.signature: Ao Nang's largest night market — street food, souvenirs, live music, a fire show on the beach, and evening lights over the sea
blocks.descHtml:
Ao Nang Landmark Night Market is the largest night market in Ao Nang, set on the beach-road along the northern Nopparat Thara Beach side — a seafront complex bringing together street food, souvenir shops, bars, a live music stage, and a seating area for an evening breeze off the water. If you're in Krabi and want a relaxed dinner stroll all in one place, this is where most people end up. The food selection runs from grilled seafood (scallops, prawns, and squid) through pad thai, pizza, and international options to dessert stalls — one lap covers all your choices.

The highlights most reviews mention are the fresh grilled seafood, which is competitively priced given the beachside setting, and mango sticky rice with fresh-pressed juice at about 50 THB a glass. Noodles and pad thai in the 70–100 THB range, pizza in the 200–220 range. After dark there is live music, traditional Thai dance, and a fire show on the beach that sets the atmosphere. The front section has bars with big screens showing sports, and a Muay Thai ring nearby. International visitor reviews mostly praise the food variety, accessible prices, and the lively scene.

Open daily from around late afternoon to approximately 23:00. The best atmosphere is after 18:00 when all the shops are fully open and shows begin. Free entry; you only pay for food and shopping. Budget around 100–300 THB per person for a comfortable evening. Located at the northern end of the Ao Nang beachfront road — walkable from the main Ao Nang beach zone, or a short songthaew ride.

Worth knowing: most stalls run on cash, so bring enough. The area is quite large and requires a fair amount of walking — wear comfortable shoes. High season evenings and nights with loud music can be crowded in some areas. For a more relaxed experience, come before the peak hours or stick to the seaside seating zone for a cooler evening with a view.
mustOrder: Grilled seafood — scallops, prawns, and squid
Mango sticky rice + fresh-pressed juice
Live music, Thai dance, and beach fire show
Evening lights by the sea
blocks.bestFor: Seaside dinner stroll — evenings out, street food lovers

blocks.name: Wat Mahathat Wachira Mongkol (Wat Bang Thong)
blocks.signature: Golden chedi over 95 meters tall, inspired by Bodh Gaya, plus a large Luang Pu Thuad image, all on over 100 rai surrounded by mountains
blocks.descHtml:
Wat Mahathat Wachira Mongkol — known locally as Wat Bang Thong — is a temple that would be a missed opportunity for anyone passing through Ao Luek. This royal monastery stands on more than 100 rai of grounds enclosed by green mountains. The golden Phra Mahathat Chedi towers approximately 95 meters — the tallest chedi in the South — designed with inspiration from the Mahabodhi Temple at Bodh Gaya, India. The scale impresses from a distance before you even step inside. Suitable for merit-makers, architectural photography enthusiasts, and families who want a peaceful stop away from the beaches.

The highlight not to miss is going inside the golden chedi itself — reviewers consistently say "far more beautiful than expected" — seeing the murals and the Buddha images decorated with extraordinary detail. Around the grounds are a large Luang Pu Thuad image, a Guan Yin Bodhisattva chedi, and various beautifully decorated structures worth a slow walk. About an hour of easy walking covers everything. The atmosphere is calm, clean, with a wide parking area and a coffee stall with drinks to rest from the heat.

Entry is free for Thais; foreign visitors typically pay a small maintenance contribution of around 50 THB. Located in Na Nuea subdistrict, Ao Luek, approximately 60–70 km from Krabi town — driving is the most practical way to get there. Open daily 08:00–18:00. Weekday mornings have fewer visitors, making it easier to walk around and photograph well.

This temple has become one of Krabi's rising landmarks — Google score 4.7 from several thousand reviews — for the beauty of the chedi and the quiet of the grounds. Dress with covered shoulders and knees; the temple provides wraps if needed. Allow extra travel time since the location is quite far from the main beaches.
mustOrder: Golden Phra Mahathat Chedi, 95 meters tall
Wall murals inside the chedi
Large Luang Pu Thuad image
Guan Yin Bodhisattva chedi
blocks.bestFor: Temple visit and architectural photography — weekday mornings

blocks.name: Krabi Walking Street
blocks.signature: City-center walking street open Fri–Sun — food stalls, seafood, souvenirs, clothing, and a live music stage in the middle of the street
blocks.descHtml:
If you happen to be in Krabi on a Friday, Saturday, or Sunday evening, Krabi Walking Street is worth a stroll. It runs through the center of town on Maharaj Road, Soi 8, next to Vogue department store — easy to walk to from most town hotels with no vehicle needed. Perfect for anyone who has been at the beach all day and wants to shift into a gentle evening mode — finding food, picking up souvenirs, and absorbing some local atmosphere. This is where locals and tourists mix, lively but never so packed that walking is uncomfortable.

The real highlight is the food — most of the tents are food vendors. Fresh seafood, pickled shrimp, cured salmon, oyster omelette, khao ho mok (steamed curry in banana leaf), pad thai, pork satay, through to desserts like mango sticky rice and an enormous variety of snacks at just a few baht each. For those who want to try something unusual, fried insects are available. Beyond the food zone there are handmade goods from local artists, hand-painted clothes, keychains, fabric bags, home goods, and a back section with vintage clothing and second-hand collectibles. Walk along far enough and you'll find live busking musicians adding energy at regular intervals.

Free entry, no ticket. A full evening including some shopping runs around 100–200 THB per person. Open Friday–Sunday evenings approximately 17:00–22:00. Worth knowing: the street is relatively compact — one full lap covers it. Expect about 1–2 hours. Do not expect a sprawling market like the big-city versions. Some chili-spiced dishes here are genuinely hot, as reviews repeatedly warn — tell the vendor if you don't eat spicy food.

What keeps the Krabi Walking Street on everyone's itinerary is its central location — walkable from town accommodation — combined with the chance to try several Southern Thai foods in one stretch and the live music stage that turns dinner into an event rather than just a meal. A good closing move for an evening in Krabi town, solo, with a partner, or with family.
mustOrder: Seafood / pickled shrimp / cured salmon
Pad thai and pork satay
Grilled potatoes
Sit and listen to live music in the street
blocks.bestFor: Weekend evening in town — relaxed stroll with food and music
blocks.spice: Some dishes are genuinely spicy — tell the vendor
blocks.libCredit: Photo: Krabi Walking Street · Christophe95 · Wikimedia Commons · CC BY-SA 4.0

blocks.name: Nopparat Thara Beach
blocks.signature: Long, quiet beach with shading trees, walk out to sea at low tide, private sunset views, and the pier for boats to the islands
blocks.priceRange: Free (national park fee applies only for island boat trips)
blocks.descHtml:
Nopparat Thara Beach — locally called Khlong Haeng Beach — is a long, quiet stretch just north of Ao Nang, inside Hat Nopparat Thara-Mu Ko Phi Phi National Park. For anyone tired of the crowds at Ao Nang, this is the answer. Fine brownish-white sand extends nearly three kilometers, with casuarina pines planted all the way along providing shade — you can sit under a tree and take the sea breeze at any time. Well suited for those who want to rest without competing for space, a quiet walk, or a family sit-down by the sea.

The highlight many visitors talk about is low tide: the beach opens up wide and you can walk into the water for hundreds of meters and still be knee-deep. Some stretches at the right tide allow you to walk out to small islets in the middle of the sea — an unusual sight and a strong photograph. The other not-to-miss moment is sunset. Late afternoon with orange light across the silhouettes of islands and longtail boats is exactly the kind of calm that Ao Nang itself doesn't always provide. Reviews consistently say come here for the sunset — more private, more atmosphere than the main beach. The pier here is also the departure point for boats to Phi Phi, Ko Poda, the Tup Islands, and other destinations.

Completely free to walk on the beach — open 24 hours, no admission fee. The park has toilets, shower facilities, a campsite, and some food stalls. The national park fee applies only when you take a boat to visit the islands. Located in Ao Nang subdistrict, about 17 km from Krabi town — drive or take a songthaew.

Worth a note: parking is limited and food options are significantly fewer than on the Ao Nang side, since everything is boat-in. Some reviews mention shell fragments and hard pieces in the sand on some stretches — walking barefoot requires some care. But for quiet, shade, and a sunset viewed without a crowd, the beach pays off for those who find it.
mustOrder: Walk into the sea at low tide
Watch the sunset under the casuarina trees
Board a boat at Nopparat Thara Pier to the islands
Sit in the shade and take in the breeze
blocks.bestFor: A quiet sunset and a walk — no crowds

blocks.name: Vogue Krabi (Vogue Department Store)
blocks.signature: Krabi's long-standing town-center department store — KFC, The Pizza Company, Watsons, Boots, a full food court, and easy parking, a reliable midday retreat from the heat
blocks.descHtml:
Vogue Krabi is the department store in Krabi town that has been with the city for over thirty years. Positioned on Maharaj Road in the old town, it's walkable from the Krabi Walking Street. For visitors who want to escape the midday heat, pick up essentials or souvenirs, or find a simple meal without thinking too hard about it, Vogue works as well for locals as it does for tourists. The building runs several floors with a shopping plaza below ground — practical rather than luxurious, but complete and easy to walk.

The highlights that bring people through: familiar brand names including KFC, The Pizza Company, Swensen's, Dairy Queen, Dunkin', and Watsons for personal care and cosmetics. The food court is on the top floor with multiple restaurants at accessible prices. The one thing reviews single out consistently is the roti stand outside Vogue — rated well as one of Krabi's top sweet spots. Fashion floors have Levi's, Giordano, Wacoal, and Guy Laroche. The underground zone sells discounted clothing, shoes, toys, and phone accessories at low prices. There's an arcade zone on the upper floor for children.

Free entry. Open daily 10:00–21:00. Easy parking. Budget per visit is flexible — food court in the tens to low hundreds of baht. Reviews praise it for value, the range of brands, and especially women's and children's clothing. Some reviews note the building is older and the selection is more limited compared to larger Bangkok malls, and a few mention staff who could be warmer. Overall, a practical drop-in for shopping, a quick meal, and shelter from the heat during a town day.
mustOrder: Roti stand outside Vogue
KFC / The Pizza Company / Swensen's
Underground discount zone
Top-floor food court
blocks.bestFor: Escape from the heat + pick up essentials and souvenirs in town

blocks.title: What to know before visiting Krabi

items.title: Getting around
items.text: For multi-zone travel, renting a car or using Grab is the most flexible option. Songthaew routes are limited. Railay Beach is accessible by boat only — from Ao Nang or Nopparat Thara Pier.

items.title: Payment
items.text: Night markets and street food at Krabi Walking Street and Ao Nang Landmark run mostly on cash. Bring small bills. Shops in malls and accommodation accept cards or QR payment.

items.title: Beat the queues
items.text: Wat Tham Suea is cooler and quieter in the early morning. Railay Beach is nicest mid-morning to early afternoon. Night markets peak in the early evening. Krabi Walking Street opens Friday–Sunday only.

items.title: Temple dress code
items.text: For Wat Tham Suea and Wat Mahathat Wachira Mongkol, dress with covered shoulders and knees and remove shoes at marked points inside the temple grounds.

items.title: Boat prices and tipping
items.text: Negotiate longtail boat fares to Khao Khanab Nam or Railay before boarding (around 170–500 THB depending on route). A small tip for a guide or boat driver is a kind gesture — never required.

items.title: Language and menus
items.text: Tourist zones like Ao Nang and Railay have English signs and menus throughout. Vendors communicate in English sufficiently. Local markets and the Krabi Walking Street may need a translation app or a point at the food.

blocks.title: Plan your Krabi trip by zone
blocks.html:
Grouping by zone saves the most time. The town zone includes Black Crab Square, Khao Khanab Nam, Vogue Krabi, and Krabi Walking Street (open Fri–Sun evenings) — these can all fit in one day. The Ao Nang zone includes Railay Beach, Nopparat Thara Beach, and Ao Nang Landmark Night Market for the evening, since they're all close together.

For nature, the Emerald Pool and Hot Springs at Khlong Thom go together in one trip — same route, usually done as a pair. Wat Tham Suea is best visited early morning to avoid climbing the 1,237 steps in midday heat. Add Wat Mahathat Wachira Mongkol at Ao Luek if you have the time — it's in that direction.

blocks.text: A well-chosen base makes Krabi over several days genuinely comfortable. Stay in Ao Nang for easy beach access and evening market walks; stay in town for the walking street and riverside landmarks. Book ahead during high season for the best prices.

faq.q: What are the must-see attractions on a first visit to Krabi?
faq.a: With limited time, collect Black Crab Square and Khao Khanab Nam — the city's defining pair of symbols — then take a longtail boat to Railay Beach with its limestone-cliff-wrapped white sand. These three are the images of Krabi that every visitor should see.

faq.q: What are the highlights of Krabi?
faq.a: Krabi stands out for its limestone mountains above water and its beautiful beaches. The top highlights are Railay Beach, Nopparat Thara Beach, and Khao Khanab Nam. For nature, the Emerald Pool and Hot Springs at Khlong Thom. For temples, Wat Tham Suea on the hilltop and the massive golden Phra Mahathat Chedi at Wat Mahathat Wachira Mongkol.

faq.q: Are entry fees expensive in Krabi?
faq.a: Most attractions on this list are free — Black Crab Square, Nopparat Thara Beach, Ao Nang Landmark Night Market, and Krabi Walking Street. The ones with costs: Emerald Pool and Hot Springs (tens to around 200 THB); Khao Khanab Nam is free to enter but requires a longtail boat hire; Railay Beach is free but needs a boat crossing.

faq.q: How do you get around Krabi and where do you park?
faq.a: For multi-zone travel, renting a car or using Grab is the most practical approach. Town spots like Black Crab Square, Vogue Krabi, and the walking street have easy parking nearby. Railay Beach is boat-access only (from Ao Nang or Nopparat Thara Pier). Longtail boat hire to Khao Khanab Nam is around 170–500 THB depending on route.

faq.q: What time do Krabi attractions open?
faq.a: Open-air landmarks and beaches — Black Crab Square, Khao Khanab Nam, Railay Beach, Nopparat Thara Beach — can be visited any time during the day through evening. Wat Tham Suea and Wat Mahathat Wachira Mongkol open during the day; go early for shade and fewer people. Krabi Walking Street opens Friday–Sunday evenings only. Ao Nang Landmark Night Market peaks after 18:00.
